chrome.code_body: In Chrome, open the tafs extension and type this code. It works for 10 minutes.
chrome.expired: The code expired, so nothing was paired. Start again.
chrome.footer: Your tafs can use a paired Chrome only on the sites a connection lists, and you approve risky steps here.
chrome.only_yours: Pair only a Chrome on a computer you're at.
chrome.profile_note: tafs works in its own Chrome profile. Sign in there only to the sites you want your tafs to use.
chrome.refused: Another Chrome used this code, so nothing was paired. Start again.
chrome.release_never_leaves: It never leaves your Chrome. tafs doesn't see it.
chrome.release_not_connected: This site isn't one you connected this Chrome to, so it can't be allowed.
chrome.release_not_https: The page isn't a secure https page, so it can't be allowed.
chrome.release_other_chrome: It's for a Chrome this phone isn't paired with, so it can't be allowed.
chrome.release_sensitive: This is a sensitive site you haven't allowed for this Chrome, so it can't be allowed.
chrome.release_unreadable: This fill can't be read, so it can't be allowed. You can still refuse it.
chrome.replace_changed: What moves to this Chrome changed, so nothing was paired. Check it and pair again.
chrome.replace_unpairs: {name} is unpaired once this one is paired.
chrome.shot_none: No picture is kept for this step.
chrome.shot_open: See the page before this step
chrome.title: Chrome
chrome.unpair_ends: Unpairing ends the connections that use it: {sites}. They come back only when you connect them again.
